cursor-fix-task.description: Phase A phase-end hardening, code wave 2 of 3: engine and CLI (sc-jev-check, sc-ai). Routine security, correctness and dead-logic fixes only. Wave 1 (foundation crates) is already on this branch at 5f94478 and added the helpers you must use: BackendId::from_str / key_id() / is_llm(), Rev::parse, JevError::encode_failed / io_failed / map_detail, ResolvedApiKey::try_new, PayloadBundle::bytes()/sha256()/into_parts(). Wave 3 (sc-treesitter, sc-jev-py) follows you.
cursor-fix-task.authoritative-review: /Volumes/Extreme Pro/github/sc-agent/PHASE-A-REVIEW.md section 3 = scope. Section 4 D1–D13 are ACCEPTED decisions but are NOT yours: a separate Phase A.1 plan implements them. In particular do NOT: change the engine entry points (D2), the session store trait/registry shape (D4), multi-backend chaining or fail-fast semantics or the equal-input computation (D3), the Extractor trait (D13), InputSpec::Command path (D11), argv parser replacement (D12), or any ADR text.

group.name: A. Security (first, each with a regression test)

items.group: - RSH-001: command extractor `Command` gets `env_clear()` plus an explicit allowlist (PATH, HOME, USERPROFILE, SYSTEMROOT, TEMP/TMP/TMPDIR, LANG, LC_*, TERM) — never any *_API_KEY or SC_* secret env. Add `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` is NOT wanted in production; keep user git config) to every git invocation in extract/read.rs, extract/mod.rs test helpers and sc-ai command.rs. Test: spawn `env`/`printenv` via a command input with a sentinel key in the parent env and assert it is absent. - RSH-002 / CR-006 / ARCHE-024: `read_worktree` canonicalizes `repo.join(relative)` and requires it `starts_with(canonicalize(repo))` and to be a regular file; reads through `take(MAX_INPUT_BYTES + 1)` and refuses oversize with InputTooLarge; `git show` output is capped the same way (or `git cat-file -s` first). Test: cfg(unix) committed symlink to a file outside the repo → InputInvalid. - RSH-003: system-prompt override read via `take(limit+1)` on a regular file; ConfigInvalid on overflow. - CR-002: `read_git_show` spec becomes `format!("{rev}:./{relative}")` so a subdirectory RepoRoot reads the same file as WORKTREE. Test with a repo root that is a subdirectory and `--rev HEAD`. - CR-007: absolutize `RepoRoot` at construction in sc-ai `resolve_repo` and anywhere the engine constructs one from user input (`std::path::absolute`, canonicalize for the git-toplevel case); `{repo_root}` substitution then cannot point at `sub/sub`. - CR-008 / ARCHE-015: `read_git_show` runs `git cat-file -t --end-of-options :./` first and requires `blob`; classify failures: bad revision → InputInvalid with the trimmed git message, path absent → InputMissing, otherwise operational io. `ExtractionFailed` carries a sanitized stderr tail (last 4 KiB, secrets redacted via JevError::map_detail path) instead of only the exit code. Replace the impossible `child.stdout/stderr.take() == None` branches with `expect`. - CR-003: single-pass placeholder substitution in payload/mod.rs (split on `{name}` tokens once, emit replacements verbatim). Test: subject text containing another input's placeholder is not re-expanded. - CR-004 / ARCHE-023: sc-ai `--check` normalised lexically (strip canonical repo prefix only for absolute args, reject `..`, convert `\` to `/`, no fs::canonicalize); engine's validate_relative + git show decide existence; reject `--rev` together with `--request-json`; pass the raw prompt-override path to the engine (stop joining it twice). - ARCHE-021: subjects extractor no longer reads process stdin for `path == "-"`; return ConfigInvalid with a hint to use `--request-json -` or a committed file. - ARCHE-008: delete `PACKAGED-PROMPT-TOKEN-a3` from assets/llm-evaluator-system.md; tests assert `PACKAGED_SYSTEM_PROMPT == include_str!(asset)` and use a prompt-override file for sentinel checks. - CR-015 / RSH-004: session `write_private` uses a unique tmp name (`.{id}.{pid}.{nonce}.tmp` via OpenOptions::create_new), removes the tmp on any error after creation, fsyncs the parent directory after rename, creates the session dir with mode 0700 on unix; document the single-writer-per-session assumption in the module doc (no advisory lock — that is a D4 decision). - CR-014: in sc-ai, a session-log flush failure after a successful run or ask is reported as a `warning` field in the envelope (or a one-line stderr note) and does not change the exit code.

- ARCHE-010 / CR-011 / RBP-F004: one `validate_question_set(&[Question])` and one `validate_state(&[ChoiceAnswer], &[Question])` in payload/questions.rs (unique ids, non-empty id/instructions, choice membership, no repeated state question) used by BOTH the check.toml path and the caller-JSON path; sc-ai and sc-jev-check parse backends via `BackendId::from_str` and revs via `Rev::parse`; registry `backend_key_id` delegates to `BackendId::key_id()`; `is_llm` copies → `BackendId::is_llm()`; `utf8_payload` single definition (pub(crate) in sc-jev-check; sc-jev-py's copy is wave 3). - ARCHE-009 / RBQA-F004 (routine part): delete `VendorPin`, `PackagedConfig.vendors`, the `[vendors.*]` tables in assets/jev.toml, `BuiltPayload.prompt`; parse the packaged jev.toml once into a `OnceLock`; `system_prompt_file` either honoured or removed (remove, since the include_str! constant is the real source; document). Keep max_input_bytes at 200000 (byte-cap owner is D13 — do not change). - ARCHE-014: keep the pre-flight `validate_for_send` (ADR-SAG-0004); drop the in-loop call when `prior` is empty (only re-validate when session context was actually appended); leave backend-internal validation alone (that is ARCHC-007 territory, done in wave 1 for backends). - ARCHE-019: `RunOptions.sessions` becomes `Option` (or a `RunOptions::dry_run()` constructor that needs neither store nor logger) so dry-run creates no `.sc-ai/`, sessions dir, or logger thread; sc-ai skips `prepare_log`/`open_sessions` on dry-run. Keep the public signature change minimal and update sc-jev-py mechanically (wave 3 may refine). - ARCHE-020: table-column extractor computes the cell's byte span in `split_row`; `producer_from_extractions` rejects more than one distinct producer with ConfigInvalid instead of silently keeping the first (making it a list is D3-adjacent; do not). - ARCHP-001 (consumer part): `validate_subjects_document` helper-capture rule checks names beginning with `_` (stored without `@`), matching the producer and the docs; fix the Rust doc comment in sc-agent-types/src/subjects.rs:64 to the same wording. - RBP-F015: replace hand-built `ConfigInvalid { detail }` / `InputInvalid { detail }` literals at run/mod.rs:252,386 and session/mod.rs:348-356 with the typed constructors (or new ones for run-request / follow-up validation) so the recovery hint matches the failure. - RBP-F002: use `JevError::encode_failed` at the five `map_err(|_| ...)` sites in sc-ai command.rs:559-607 and any sc-jev-check equivalents; use `io_failed` where io errors are currently stringified. - CR-012: fix the `extract/subjects.rs` rustdoc to say ExtractionInvalid (the code is right). - CR-016 / ARCHE-018 (bug part only; keep the custom parser): `--flag=value` accepts values starting with `-`; `--help`/`-h` only recognised in argument positions 1–2; keep flag tables as they are otherwise (clap is D12).

- ARCHE-016 / RBP-F015 / QA-007 / ARCHP-021: move `src/run/exact.rs` to `tests/sessions_exact.rs` (drop the `a6_exact` [[test]] stanza), deduplicate the tests it repeats from run/mod.rs and session/mod.rs; `tempfile::TempDir` replaces the three hand-rolled temp-dir helpers in sc-jev-check and the one in sc-ai tests; consolidate the five ad-hoc JudgeBackend doubles onto `ScriptedJudge` (add request capture to it if needed — it lives in sc-jev-check under test-util, keep it there; moving it is D7/ARCHC-010) and delete the copies; remove the lib.rs "Sprint a-1 freezes this mod list" comment (replace with a one-line pointer to docs/architecture.md); split inline test modules over ~400 lines into `run/tests.rs` / `session/tests.rs`. - ARCHE-017 / RBQA-F011: make pub(crate): PayloadBuilder, refuse_over_cap, parse_state, STATE_SCHEMA, the four extractor structs, read_repo_bytes/text, parse_subjects_bytes, validate_subjects_document, equal_input::{record, commands_for, same_bytes, producer_from_extractions}, render_session_context, FileSessionStore::load_raw, registry::backend_key_id — EXCEPT anything sc-ai, sc-jev-py, tests/jev_cross_impl or crates/sc-jev-check/tests actually import (grep first; keep those pub and list them in your report). Move `prepare_caller_request` / `PreparedCallerRequest` into payload/ (re-export from run so callers do not change). In sc-ai lib.rs stop re-exporting observe items and gate `ExecuteOverrides` behind `#[doc(hidden)]` + a `test-support` feature used only by sc-ai's own tests (EXT-003 CLI half). Update `boundaries/sc-jev-check/jev-check.toml` and `boundaries/sc-ai/sc-ai-cli.toml` facade strings to match (these two manifest edits are allowed in this wave; the docs branch already rewrote them so keep the edit minimal and mention it). - CR-013: extend tests/fixtures/jev/cross_impl/logical.json with `\n`, `\t`, `"`, `\\`, `/`, `\u001f`, DEL, U+2028, a non-BMP emoji, and non-ASCII and `"￿"` object keys; regenerate reference.bytes/reference.sha256 with `canonicalize.py --write`; both Rust and Python cross-impl tests must still pass. - FTQ-003: a `spawn_with_deadline` test helper in sc-ai tests/cli.rs (try_wait polling, 60 s, kill+reap, panic with stderr) used by every subprocess test; `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` (or NUL on Windows) and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` on test git helpers. - QA-005: no rustdoc warnings in sc-jev-check or sc-ai (`cargo doc -p sc-jev-check -p sc-ai --no-deps`).

cursor-fix-task.acceptance-criteria: - `just lint`, `just test`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` (warning count ≤ the 6 wave 1 left, all in sc-treesitter/sc-jev-py) green; `cargo test --workspace` passes including sc-jev-py and tests/jev_cross_impl after your signature changes (mechanical call-site fixes in sc-jev-py are allowed, nothing else there). - Every security item has a test that fails without the fix. - `bash scripts/sc-publish-dry-run.sh` still exits 0 (you are not changing crate layout, so it should). - No D1–D13 scope entered; no ADR text; no kit-written files; boundary manifest edits limited to the two facade strings. - Commit per group (A, B, C), push, report pushed SHA, per-item status table (done / deferred+reason), validation table, the list of items you kept `pub` because a consumer imports them, and anything you believe is an architectural decision in disguise.

workflow.step: ACK. `git pull --ff-only` the branch first (wave 1 is on origin). Work only in the worktree; zsh: never use a variable named `status`.
Read PHASE-A-REVIEW.md sections 3–4, the reviewer JSON for your ids, then sc-jev-check and sc-ai fully.
Implement A → B → C, `cargo test --workspace` after each group.
Commit per group with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 `, push, report. No PR, no merge, no agents.
